claims.statement: `langgraph.json` registers three specialized review graphs: `reviewer`, `analyzer`, and `review-scout`, respectively pointing to traced graph factories under `agent.graphs`.

The reviewer graph is repository-read-only: its configured tool list contains finding/review publication and read helpers but no coding, commit, push, or PR-opening tool; publication is its controlled GitHub mutation boundary.

The reviewer factory copies the config and configurable mapping before setting a default recursion limit, whereas the analyzer factory sets the default recursion limit on its incoming config; both return an empty tool-less deep agent if no thread ID is supplied or execution is disabled.

Reviewer preparation obtains a repository-scoped App token for source runs, caches it as a bot token, creates a replaceable sandbox, checks out the PR head, and materializes trusted skills from the base SHA; replacement failure posts an unreachable-sandbox notification before failing the run.

Reviewer run preparation computes a full or delta re-review diff and changed-line set, passes them in state for finding validation, and concurrently fetches PR context, review threads, style/guidance/instructions, standards, and scout-derived context.

`add_finding` validates finding fields and resolves diff context from injected state, configuration, then a fresh authenticated PR diff; an out-of-diff anchor returns an explicit non-retryable failure, while successful additions retain a hunk when available and use fingerprint-based idempotent persistence.

Canonical reviewer findings and interactions are stored as PostgreSQL rows under a pull request, while LangGraph reviewer-thread metadata holds PR identity and lifecycle/routing fields including mandatory `kind: reviewer`.

First access to a legacy reviewer thread backfills metadata findings into PostgreSQL exactly once via a pull-request state row; finding mutations lock that state row and reread latest rows, and concurrent identical additions resolve idempotently by fingerprint.
A missing reviewer LangGraph thread is exposed to tools as a structured `thread_not_found` do-not-retry result rather than an empty findings result.

GitHub publication requires an exact ranking, posts eligible in-diff open findings, records publication identities, resolves threads, advances reviewer metadata, and returns structured empty re-review and dry-run outcomes that do not imply a new GitHub review.

Inline review comments embed an `open-swe-review-comment` marker; subsequent reconciliation matches markers before stored identities, backfills GitHub IDs, records human replies for reassessment, and resolves findings only when every matched thread is resolved.

The analyzer mounts bundled mode playbooks as virtual `/skills/` files and has only `save_review_style_prompt` and `read_finding_outcomes` as domain tools; bootstrap and continual launch paths use a deterministic per-repository review-style thread.

A `ReviewStyle` record in the typed `review_styles` store contains the learned prompt, analysis status and metadata, run/thread and cron identifiers, error, and timestamps; reviewer prompt lookup fails soft when that store is unavailable.

Saving a nonempty learned style marks the record completed and attempts idempotent continual-cron registration; per-repository cron schedules are deterministically staggered between 05:00 and 08:59 UTC and explicitly configure the deterministic analyzer thread for otherwise threadless executions.
The review scout starts or joins a run per PR head, waits at most 600 seconds for an exact-head PostgreSQL walkthrough and otherwise lets review proceed; a newer head supersedes older scout work.

The scout uses only walkthrough-commit and guidance-recording tools, replaces a head- and merge-base-pinned PostgreSQL walkthrough after finalization, and records author guidance only when its quote matches stored human steering; guidance is upserted by quote and visible only for the latest completed scout head.

Watch-mode webhook tests verify that re-review requires a watching reviewer thread and a changed head/diff, persists the live head for queued runs, and disables or re-enables watch when a PR closes or reopens.
